note: Anti-PD-1 antibodies entered relapsed cHL on 9p24.1/PD-L1 tumour genomics rather than an animal model of the disease; nivolumab led, followed by sintilimab, camrelizumab, tislelizumab, penpulimab and zimberelimab in China.
label: Hodgkin lymphoma (anti-PD-1)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Opening year 2006 is a proxy for first-in-human (MDX-1106-01), when the binding data were already in hand; the paper is 2014.
engagement.model: Ex-vivo PD-1 binding on activated human T cells
engagement.note: Nivolumab bound PD-1 on activated human T cells and blocked ligand binding; occupancy in dosed humans not yet reported.
engagement.quote: Nivolumab binds to PD-1 with high affinity and specificity, and effectively inhibits the interaction between PD-1 and its ligands.
engagement.judgement: Opening proxy at first use; the ex-vivo assay is the system the FDA review says set the starting dose.

engagement.magnitude_basis: PD-1 occupancy on circulating T cells after a single dose
engagement.population: Refractory solid tumours (occupancy readout; not cHL)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Patients had solid tumours (melanoma, CRC, CRPC, NSCLC, RCC), not cHL; occupancy is a T-cell readout independent of tumour type.
engagement.model: Ex-vivo PD-1 binding on activated human T cells
engagement.note: Single nivolumab doses of 0.3-10 mg/kg held >70% PD-1 occupancy on circulating T cells for 2 months or more.
engagement.quote: However, pharmacodynamics indicated a sustained mean occupancy of > 70% of PD-1 molecules on circulating T cells ≥ 2 months following infusion, regardless of dose.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: model side Wang 2014 (published 2014, so the pairing dates 2014), patient side Brahmer 2010. Readout is receptor occupancy on the cells the assay used, so direct. No cHL-specific occupancy study found; the FDA 2015 review restates both sides (trough >160x binding EC50) without changing status.

dose.confidence_note: Opening year is a proxy for first-in-human; the model data are known only from the FDA review.
dose.model: Mouse syngeneic tumour PK-PD (MC38, Sa1/N) with ex-vivo binding EC50
dose.note: Sponsor's mouse tumour PK-PD (10-30 mg/kg efficacious) scaled to a predicted active human dose; not public before the 2015 review.
dose.quote: Second, the clinical dose of 3 mg/kg was selected based on PK-PD studies in animals.
dose.judgement: Opening proxy. The mouse models used a surrogate antibody (nivolumab does not bind mouse PD-1), so product_in_model false; that is my inference, the review does not say.

dose.magnitude_basis: predicted minimum active human dose (~1 mg/kg) vs lowest dose with clinical activity and saturating occupancy (1 mg/kg; occupancy plateau from 0.3 mg/kg)
dose.population: Solid tumours (PK); cHL dosed at the same regimen
dose.confidence_note: Patient PK in the review is from solid tumours (MDX1106-03, CA209063); cHL patients in CheckMate 039/205 received the same 3 mg/kg Q2W. The review's own wording runs across a page break.
dose.model: Mouse syngeneic tumour PK-PD (MC38, Sa1/N) with ex-vivo binding EC50
dose.note: Model predicted blockade and activity from about 1 mg/kg; 3 mg/kg Q2W reached troughs >160x binding EC50, the dose then used in cHL.
dose.quote: Based on the human equivalent dose calculations, the sponsor predicted nivolumab to demonstrate PD-1 blockade and clinical activity at doses of approximately 1 mg/kg or higher in humans.
dose.judgement: The model stated an exposure target (HED of ~1 mg/kg); patients were dosed at 3 mg/kg with troughs >16 ug/mL and MTD not reached at 10 mg/kg, so the target half is same. No tolerability margin was stated by this system, so margin_stated false. Whether 3 mg/kg worked in cHL is the efficacy question.

efficacy.model: cHL cell lines and microdissected Reed-Sternberg cells (9p24.1/PD-L1/PD-L2 genomics)
efficacy.note: 9p24.1 amplification raised PD-L1/PD-L2 in Hodgkin cell lines and primary HRS cells, nominating PD-1 blockade; no patient dosed yet.
efficacy.quote: Therefore, 9p24.1 amplification is a disease-specific structural alteration that increases both the gene dosage of PD-1 ligands and their induction by JAK2, defining the PD-1 pathway and JAK2 as complementary rational therapeutic targets.
efficacy.judgement: No animal model of cHL was relied on; the class entered cHL on this tumour-genomic rationale, recorded as an ex-vivo system without drug exposure.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: objective response rate vs a qualitative prediction of sensitivity
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Phase 1 (NCT01592370, CheckMate 039) with safety and efficacy as objectives; registrational CheckMate 205 confirmed.
efficacy.model: cHL cell lines and microdissected Reed-Sternberg cells (9p24.1/PD-L1/PD-L2 genomics)
efficacy.note: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg gave 87% objective response in heavily treated relapsed cHL; all ten tested tumours carried PD-L1/PD-L2 copy gains.
efficacy.quote: An objective response was reported in 20 patients (87%), including 17% with a complete response and 70% with a partial response; the remaining 3 patients (13%) had stable disease.
efficacy.judgement: The paper sets the 9p24.1 rationale beside the response and the tumour copy gains, so comparison_stated true. Endpoint taken as primary because the study's stated objectives were safety and efficacy together; CheckMate 205's primary ORR (66%) and sintilimab's ORIENT-1 are listed as confirming trials. Magnitude direction only: the genomic model gave no response rate.

patient_trials.quote: Malignant cells of classical Hodgkin's lymphoma are characterised by genetic alterations at the 9p24.1 locus, leading to overexpression of PD-1 ligands and evasion of immune surveillance.
Sintilimab (Innovent Biologics, Suzhou, China), a highly selective, fully humanised, monoclonal antibody, blocks the interaction between PD-1 and its ligands.

efficacy.note: FISH graded 9p24.1 alterations (polysomy, gain, amplification) in 108 cHL biopsies and called for testing in checkpoint-treated patients.
efficacy.quote: Further analyses of 9p24.1 alterations in patients treated with standard cHL induction regimens or checkpoint blockade are warranted.
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level track: does the grade of 9p24.1 alteration pick responders. Kept apart from the cell-line track because the system is a diagnostic FISH assay on patient tissue.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Association with PFS, not with the trial's primary ORR; complete remission tracked MHC class II rather than 9p24.1 in the abstract.
efficacy.note: In CheckMate 205, higher-level 9p24.1 gain and PD-L1 expression on HRS cells went with longer PFS on nivolumab; MHC class II predicted complete remission.
efficacy.quote: Patients with higher-level 9p24.1 copy gain and increased PD-L1 expression on HRS cells had superior PFS.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: scored same with source_calls_it partial, because the assay predicted PFS in the direction expected but the abstract does not report it predicting objective response or complete remission. Comparison stated by the paper itself.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; doses not given in the abstract. Opening year is a proxy for first-in-human.
safety.note: Nivolumab at high doses produced no immune-related adverse events in cynomolgus monkeys.
safety.quote: Nivolumab treatment did not induce adverse immune-related events when given to cynomolgus macaques at high concentrations, independent of circulating anti-nivolumab antibodies where observed.
safety.judgement: Opening proxy at first use; the monkey studies were filed with the IND/BLA.

safety.magnitude_basis: immune-related adverse events: none in monkeys vs serious colitis in patients
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Patient side is from solid tumours (imported); cHL labels carry the same immune-mediated warnings but I did not quote a cHL-specific source.
safety.note: Monkeys showed no immune-related harm; patients developed immune-mediated colitis from the first phase 1, later pneumonitis and other immune-mediated reactions.
safety.short: Silent on immune toxicity seen in patients
safety.quote: Anti-PD-1 was well tolerated: one serious adverse event, inflammatory colitis, was observed in a patient with melanoma who received five doses at 1 mg/kg.
safety.judgement: Judgement call: cynomolgus monkeys can show immune-mediated colitis (seen with anti-CTLA-4), so the model's silence on immune-related events is a miss, not a species limit. Paired by me (model side Wang 2014, so dated 2014); patient comparison imported from melanoma.

safety.model: Mouse allogeneic bone-marrow transplant GVHD models with PD-1 pathway blockade
safety.note: Blocking PD-1 engagement markedly accelerated GVHD lethality in several mouse transplant models.
safety.quote: In each, GVHD lethality was markedly accelerated.
safety.judgement: A harm relevant to cHL, where PD-1 blockade often precedes allogeneic transplant. Anti-mouse PD-1 / PD-L1 reagents, not a member drug.

safety.population: Relapsed/refractory lymphoma (mostly cHL) undergoing allogeneic HSCT after PD-1 blockade
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; retrospective series without a control arm; prior antibodies include pembrolizumab (not a member) as well as nivolumab, and I did not confirm the split from the abstract.
safety.model: Mouse allogeneic bone-marrow transplant GVHD models with PD-1 pathway blockade
safety.note: Lymphoma patients (mostly cHL) transplanted after PD-1 blockade had 23% grade 3-4 acute GVHD, three early GVHD deaths and a steroid-requiring febrile syndrome.
safety.quote: However, there may be an increased risk of early immune toxicity, which could reflect long-lasting immune alterations triggered by prior PD-1 blockade.
safety.judgement: Judgement call: the mice received PD-1 blockade at transplant, patients weeks before it; scored same because the predicted harm (accelerated GVHD) appeared, direction only. Paired by me; model side Blazar 2003. FDA later added a GVHD warning to the cHL label.

safety.model: PD-1 knockout mice (spontaneous lupus-like autoimmunity, GVH-like disease)
safety.note: PD-1-null mice developed lupus-like arthritis and glomerulonephritis, predicting immune-mediated harm from losing PD-1 signalling; no patient dosed yet.
safety.short: PD-1 loss causes autoimmunity in mice
safety.quote: Aged C57BL/6(B6)-PD-1(-/-) congenic mice spontaneously developed characteristic lupus-like proliferative arthritis and glomerulonephritis with predominant IgG3 deposition
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; opening entry at first use.

safety.model: PD-1 knockout mice (spontaneous lupus-like autoimmunity, GVH-like disease)
safety.note: In 263 nivolumab-treated cHL patients the label reports immune-mediated pneumonitis, thyroiditis, colitis and other immune-mediated reactions, as PD-1 loss in mice foretold.
safety.quote: Immune-mediated pneumonitis occurred in 3.4% (9/263) of patients receiving OPDIVO (one Grade 3 and eight Grade 2).
safety.confidence_note: Label read in full (pdftotext). Knockout organ pattern (arthritis, nephritis) differs from the patients' (pneumonitis, thyroiditis, colitis); scored on the class of harm.
safety.judgement: Paired by me: knockout mice predicted immune-mediated disorders in general, and cHL patients had them; direction only, since organs differ. The label cites knockout autoimmunity only under pregnancy, so not a stated comparison. Earliest cHL-specific immune-mediated rates found are this May 2016 label (Trials 8 and 9).
safety.population: Relapsed/refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma after autologous HSCT (CheckMate 205 and 039)

safety.note: Run after capillary haemangioma was seen in camrelizumab patients: screen found off-target VEGFR2 agonism, offered as the cause.
safety.quote: SHR-1210 was found to be a potent agonist of human VEGFR2, which may thereby drive hemangioma development via vascular endothelial cell activation.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; opening entry at first use (epub 12 Dec 2018).
safety.model: Human cell-surface receptor proteome screen and VEGFR2 agonism assay for camrelizumab (SHR-1210)

safety.note: In the camrelizumab cHL phase 2, cutaneous reactive capillary endothelial proliferation occurred in 97% of patients, the harm the VEGFR2 screen reproduced.
safety.quote: The most common ones included cutaneous reactive capillary endothelial proliferation (97.3%, 73/75) and pyrexia (42.7%, 32/75).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both. Finlay's patient reference is to camrelizumab patients generally (solid tumours); the cHL incidence comes from Song 2019. Registry results posting for the phase 2 (NCT03155425) not found; registry_date null.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: haemangiomas were known in patients before the screen was run, so retro, not same. Scored as an off-target harm of this member only. Paired by me with the cHL trial; the model paper itself states the patient harm.
safety.population: Chinese patients with relapsed/refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma
safety.model: Human cell-surface receptor proteome screen and VEGFR2 agonism assay for camrelizumab (SHR-1210)
